title: Talking About the Past: Was and Were
summary: Learn how to use 'was' and 'were' to talk about the past. You will be able to describe where you were and how you felt yesterday.

sections.p: 'Was' is the past form of 'am' and 'is'. We use 'was' with singular words like I, he, she, and it. Use 'was' when you talk about one person, one place, or one thing in the past. For example, you can talk about where you were yesterday or how you felt last week.

ex.mean: At my house on the day before today

ex.en: She was happy with her gift.
The weather was cold this morning.

sections.p: 'Were' is the past form of 'are'. We use 'were' with plural words like we, you, and they. Use 'were' when you talk about two or more people, places, or things in the past. Remember to always use 'were' with the word 'you', even when you talk to only one person.

ex.en: We were at the park last night.
ex.mean: At the outdoor public space yesterday evening

ex.en: You were late for the meeting.
They were very tired after work.

sections.p: To make a negative sentence, just add 'not' after 'was' or 'were'. We often use short forms to speak faster and more naturally in everyday conversation. Say 'wasn't' instead of 'was not', and say 'weren't' instead of 'were not'.

ex.mean: Did not want to eat food

ex.en: They weren't ready for the test.
ex.mean: Did not prepare for the exam

tip: Think of 'I', 'he', 'she', and 'it' as single friends who like 'was'. Think of 'we', 'you', and 'they' as groups that like 'were'.

quiz.en: They ___ at the supermarket last night.
She ___ not happy with the service.
We ___ late because of the traffic.
You ___ great at the presentation yesterday.
